families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer films combined with retained acid or DES motifs aim to keep a hydrogen-bonded proton phase continuous through the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: DES or retained acid can preserve bound polar-fluid continuity at low temperature.
D3: plasticised biopolymer hosts are plausible flexible scaffolds below freezing by analogy to hydrated chitosan/starch films.
D6: starch, chitosan, and PVA supply dense OH/NH hydrogen-bond sites for proton relay.
D7: chitosan and low-loaded phosphoric acid are reported to retain the conducting phase without membrane collapse.

families.family_description: One-dimensional clay hosts confine and retain phosphoric-acid-rich domains while guiding interconnected proton-transport channels in soft matrices.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric acid in complexed or confined form is supported as a non-neat proton source.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite nanotubes provide nanoconfinement and channel guidance.
D7: clay hosts are reported to reduce acid leaching and improve phase retention.
D6: phosphoric acid supplies hydrogen-bond-mediated proton transfer when retained in the composite.

families.family_description: Amorphous phosphate-rich networks offer non-crystalline proton-conducting media with strong hydrogen-bond structure and intrinsic confinement.
descriptor_match: D1: protonated phosphate glass is reported as an amorphous continuous transport medium.
D4: phosphate-rich acid environments are analogous to non-crystallising proton sources under confinement.
D6: phosphate networks provide strong hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor environments for proton relay.
D7: phosphate glass intrinsically retains the conducting phase, though long-term conductivity stability can be conditional.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan-rich film-forming matrix blended with PVA and loaded with 1D attapulgite carrying retained phosphoric acid.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity in an OH-rich flexible matrix
nanoconfinement: 1D clay can organize interconnected acid pathways
retention: chitosan plus attapulgite should suppress phosphoric-acid loss
risk_flags: PA overloading may increase leaching or brittleness
cold flexibility is inferred rather than directly measured
instances.novelty_rationale: This combines the supported chitosan-attapulgite confinement motif with a PVA film former and free phosphoric acid rather than the reported PWA-containing composite. The quaternary design directly targets cold-side continuity using an OH-rich host plus 1D confinement.

instances.composition_description: A starch-PVA blend film incorporating halloysite nanotubes preloaded or contacted with phosphoric acid to create confined acid channels.
expected_properties: cold_window: starch/PVA hydrogen-bond network may retain bound polar continuity
nanoconfinement: HNT lumen and surface can host acid and limit leaching
proton_transfer: phosphoric-acid-rich confined domains should support hybrid hopping/vehicular transport
risk_flags: starch-rich films may swell excessively at high humidity
PA-HNT loading balance may be hard to optimize
instances.novelty_rationale: The instance merges a known starch/PVA hydrogen-bonded host with HNT-based acid confinement not reported together in the provided pool. It is novel because each element is supported separately, but the integrated cold-oriented architecture is only analogous.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane plasticised with a choline-chloride/phosphoric-acid deep eutectic to provide a retained acid-like conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: DES motif is plausible for non-crystallising bound-fluid continuity near 200 K
flexibility: DES-plasticised chitosan should reduce glassy disconnects
retention: chitosan can hold high polar-phase uptake without disintegration
risk_flags: high DES content may soften the film too much
instances.novelty_rationale: This retains the supported chitosan-DES route but specifies a ChCl/PA acid DES as the plasticising proton medium. The novelty lies in translating the DES evidence toward a colder, phosphoric-acid-centered composition rather than a generic DES blend.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous phosphate glass with proton-substituted phosphate network functionality used as the primary proton-conducting phase.
components: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
expected_properties: pathway_continuity: amorphous network directly supports continuous proton transport
noncrystalline_phase: no freezing of a separate water phase is required
retention: conducting species are intrinsically immobilised within the glass network
risk_flags: conductivity stability can depend on water-state control

element_evidence.component: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)

instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a control because the descriptor match is direct rather than combinatorial. It provides a benchmark for amorphous continuous transport without relying on soft-matter confinement.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan host loaded with phosphoric-acid-filled halloysite nanotubes to couple biopolymer retention with tubular nanoconfinement.
expected_properties: retention: chitosan plus HNTs should reduce acid leakage
nanoconfinement: tubular clay can maintain connected confined proton domains
cold_window: bound acid in an OH-rich host is plausible below freezing
risk_flags: interfacial dispersion of HNTs may be uneven
acid content may trade off against mechanical integrity
instances.novelty_rationale: This hybridizes the chitosan retention scaffold with the HNT phosphoric-acid confinement motif, a pairing not explicitly present in the claim pool. The design is a concise cold-oriented analogue of the stronger clay-confined acid concepts.
